technology_name: Advanced Electrode Platform for Fast-Charging Supercapacitors: TiO2 Nanotube Arrays
institution: KSCSTE - Srinivasa Ramanujan Institute for Basic Sciences
problem_solved: The need for scalable, high-performance, and cyclically stable electrodes with high energy and power densities for next-generation fast-charging supercapacitors.
description: A novel temperature-controlled water bath anodization technique to synthesize high-performance TiO2 nanotube array (TNTA) electrodes. This approach induces in-situ crystallization, forming a mixed-phase structure (monoclinic TiO2(B) and orthorhombic Brookite) that supports both pseudocapacitive ion intercalation and surface redox reactions. The technology utilizes high oxygen vacancies and doping strategies, achieving outstanding specific capacitance (up to 916.27 F/g) and massive energy densities (up to 509 Wh/kg).
applications:
• Manufacturing of next-generation fast-charging supercapacitors

• Advanced energy storage systems for electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid power grids

• High-performance power components for portable electronics and medical devices

• Commercial nanomaterial synthesis and electrode fabrication pipelines
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, MedTech & Health Care
